DC-2025-B260697.aiSummary: This bill would change many reporting rules for the District Department of Energy and Environment and related laws. It would replace some report handoffs to the Council with posting the reports on agency websites, change deadlines, and make some reports less frequent or cover longer time spans. It would also end some outdated or repeated reporting rules.

DC-2025-B260848.title: Private Vehicle-for-Hire Operator Clarification Congressional Review Emergency Amendment Act of 2026

actions.text: Returned from Mayor
Transmitted to Mayor, Response Due on Nov 02, 2026
Retained by the Council
Final Reading, CC
B26-0848 Introduced by Councilmember Nadeau at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-B260848.aiSummary: The measure would make an emergency change to D.C. rules for for-hire vehicles and clarify who counts as a private vehicle-for-hire operator. It says this is a person who uses a company’s digital dispatch system to drive a motor vehicle and give rides to passengers. The change would apply as of March 1, 2024.

DC-2025-B260840.title: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Stadium-Armory Station Improvements Fiscal Year 2026 to Fiscal Year 2030 Reimbursable Agreement Emergency Act of 2026

actions.text: Returned from Mayor
Transmitted to Mayor, Response Due on Nov 04, 2026
Retained by the Council with comments from the Committee on Transportation and the Environment
Final Reading
B26-0840 Introduced by Chairman Mendelson at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-B260840.aiSummary: The Council would approve an emergency, multiyear reimbursable agreement with the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority to design and build station improvements at the Stadium-Armory Metrorail Station. The agreement would cover fiscal years 2026 through 2030 and total $300 million. The act would take effect after mayoral approval or a council override and last for up to 90 days.

DC-2025-B260444.aiSummary: The act changes the Food Policy Council’s report schedule from every year to every 3 years, starting September 30, 2027. It also gives the council more power to review food buying by District agencies and contractors that regularly buy food and drinks, and to set food purchasing standards and data-sharing rules. The changes apply to covered agencies and to the Office of Contracting and Procurement.

DC-2025-B260826.title: Alternative Breakfast Service Model Temporary Amendment Act of 2026

actions.text: Transmitted to Mayor, Response Due on Nov 12, 2026
Final Reading, CC
Retained by the Council
First Reading
B26-0826 Introduced by Councilmember Parker at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-B260826.aiSummary: The bill would change the rules for school breakfast in the District on a temporary basis. It would let schools use grab-and-go breakfast, breakfast served in the classroom, or both. The change would apply to District school breakfast service and would last for 225 days after it takes effect.
